sense: bring up children or young animals

evidence: Varr. in Non. 447.33: ēducit obstetrīx, ēducat nūtrīx, īnstituit paedagōgus, docet magister (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The whole upbringing of a child, body and mind. Not to be confused with ēdūcō, ēdūcere (long ū, third conjugation), “lead out”, which can also mean rear (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plaut. Rud. 3.4.36 (Lewis & Short, s.v. ēducō): Athēnīs nātus altusque ēducātusque Atticīs
terms.comment: To feed and keep a child or an animal; nātus altusque, born and bred. Also of keeping animals (canēs alere).

phrases.latin: vidēn tū puerum hunc … quem tam humilī cultū ēducāmus?
phrases.english: do you see this boy, whom we are bringing up in such a humble way?

phrases.latin: in hujus sinū indulgentiāque ēducātus per omnem honestārum artium cultum pueritiam adulēscentiamque trānsēgit
phrases.english: brought up in her lap and in her care, he spent his boyhood and youth in the study of every liberal art

sources: Lewis & Short: educo · Lewis & Short: alo
